sub.label: Project Summary
prompts: Provide a brief overview of your project. Reference the Abstract from Part A.

sub.label: 1.1 Background and general objectives
prompts: Describe the background and rationale of the project.
How is the project relevant to the scope of the call?
How does the project address the general objectives of the call?
What is the project's contribution to the priorities of the call?
Which target groups will be supported/assisted by/in the project? Why have you chosen to focus on them?

sub.label: 1.2 Needs analysis and specific objectives
prompts: Provide a needs assessment. A need is a gap between what is and what should/would be helpful or useful.
Specify what needs will be addressed and how they have been identified.
Demonstrate the need for the action using relevant, reliable data and robust analysis.
Incorporate gender equality issues and non-discrimination considerations.
Provide data disaggregated by sex, age or disability whenever possible.
If your project is supported by a public authority, annex the Letter of support.

sub.label: 1.3 Complementarity with other actions and innovation - European added value
prompts: Explain how the project builds on the results of past activities carried out in the field.
Describe the innovative aspects of the project.
Explain how the activities are complementary to other activities carried out by other organisations.
Illustrate the European dimension: trans-national dimension, impact for multiple EU countries, potential for cross-border cooperation.
Which countries will benefit from the project and why have you chosen them?
Clarify how the project builds on synergies with other EU projects and previous project results.
How does your project complement Member States' interventions in gender equality and non-discrimination mainstreaming?

sub.label: 2.1 Concept and methodology
prompts: Outline the approach and methodology behind the project.
Explain why this approach is the most suitable for achieving the project's objectives.
Include ethical and safety considerations to ensure that target groups are not subjected to harm.
Note: Methodology is not a list of activities but instruments and approaches that will be used and applied.

sub.label: 2.2 Consortium set-up
prompts: Describe the participants (Beneficiaries, Affiliated Entities and Associated Partners, if any).
Explain how they will work together to implement the project.
How will they bring together the necessary expertise? How will they complement each other?
Show that each participant has a valid role and adequate resources to fulfil that role.
Note: For Town Twinning and Programme Contact Points, this section may not apply.

sub.label: 2.3 Project teams, staff and experts
prompts: Describe the project teams and how they will work together to implement the project.
List the staff included in the project budget by function/profile (e.g. project manager, senior expert, junior expert, trainers/teachers, technical personnel, administrative personnel).
Describe briefly their tasks. Provide CVs of all key actors if required.
Ensure a gender-balanced representation in the composition of project teams and staff.
Describe how you intend to get outside resources: contributions of members, partner organisations, volunteers, subcontracting, etc.
If there is subcontracting, complete the table in section 4. Ensure subcontractors are aware of gender mainstreaming and non-discrimination mainstreaming.

sub.label: 2.4 Consortium management and decision-making
prompts: Explain the management structures and decision-making mechanisms within the consortium.
Describe how decisions will be taken and how regular and effective communication will be ensured.
Describe methods to ensure planning and control.
The management structure must be adapted to the complexity and scale of the project.
Note: For Town Twinning and Programme Contact Points, this section may not apply.

sub.label: 2.5 Project management, quality assurance and monitoring and evaluation strategy
prompts: Describe the measures planned to ensure that the project implementation is of high quality and completed in time.
Describe the methods to ensure good quality, monitoring, planning and control.
Describe the evaluation methods and indicators (quantitative and qualitative) to monitor and verify the outreach and coverage of the activities and results.
Propose indicators that are relevant, realistic and measurable, with unit of measurement, baseline and target values.
Incorporate gender and non-discrimination considerations in monitoring and evaluation.
Ensure indicators are gender responsive and can measure gender equality changes over time.
The evaluation should be participatory and inclusive to all stakeholders.

sub.label: 2.6 Cost effectiveness and financial management
prompts: Describe the measures adopted to ensure that the proposed results and objectives will be achieved in the most cost-effective way.
Indicate how the financial resources will be allocated and managed within the consortium based on the distribution and implementation of the tasks.
Present cost effectiveness measures per cost categories (e.g. staff profiles adapted to tasks, subcontracting costs estimated based on recent offers).
Note: Not applicable for prefixed Lump Sum Grants.

sub.label: 2.7 Risk management
prompts: Describe critical risks, uncertainties or difficulties related to the implementation of your project.
Present your measures and strategy for addressing them.
For each risk, indicate the impact and likelihood that the risk will materialise (high, medium, low), even after mitigating measures.
Include risk mitigation measures that address gender inequalities and multiple discriminatory effects in project implementation.
Identify accessibility barriers, language barriers, and childcare provision constraints that may affect participation.
Note: Not applicable for Town Twinning.

sub.label: 3.1 Impact and ambition
prompts: Define the short, medium and long-term effects of the project.
Who are the target groups? How will they benefit concretely from the project?
What would change for them? In what way will the identified gap be reduced?
How will the activities contribute to improve the situation (difference between starting point and situation after the end of the project)?
How will the activities contribute to the promotion and advancement of gender equality and non-discrimination mainstreaming?
Does the project aim to trigger change or innovation? Describe them and the degree of ambition.

Note: Results/outcomes are immediate changes for target groups after the end of the project (improved knowledge, increased awareness). Deliverables are activities undertaken and outputs produced with allocated resources.

sub.label: 3.2 Communication, dissemination and visibility
prompts: Describe the communication and dissemination activities planned to promote the activities/results and maximise the impact.
To whom will you communicate? What format and how many activities?
How will you reach the target groups, relevant stakeholders, policymakers and the general public?
Explain the choice of dissemination channels.
Describe how the visibility of EU funding will be ensured.
Communication activities should contribute to the promotion of gender equality and non-discrimination.
Use gender inclusive language and positive visual representations in communication materials.
Ensure that communication channels are accessible to general audience, particularly persons with disabilities and marginalised groups.

sub.label: 3.3 Sustainability and continuation
prompts: Describe the follow-up of the project after the EU funding ends.
How will the project impact be ensured and sustained?
What will need to be done? Which parts of the project should be continued or maintained?
How will this be achieved? Which resources will be necessary to continue the project?
How will the results be used?
Are there any possible synergies/complementarities with other (EU funded) activities that can build on the project results?

sections.label: 4. Workplan, Work Packages, Activities, Resources and Timing

sub.label: 4.1 Work plan
prompts: Provide a brief description of the overall structure of the work plan.
You may use a list of work packages or a graphical presentation (PERT chart or similar).

sub.label: 4.2 Work packages, activities, resources and timing
prompts: Group your activities into work packages. A work package means a major sub-division of the project.
For each work package, enter an objective (expected outcome) and list the activities, milestones and deliverables that belong to it.
The grouping should be logical and guided by identifiable outputs.

Projects should normally have a minimum of 2 work packages. WP1 should cover the management and coordination activities (meetings, coordination, project monitoring and evaluation, financial management, progress reports) and all cross-cutting activities.
WP2 and further WPs should cover the other project activities. You can create as many work packages as needed.
For very simple projects, use a single work package for the entire project.
For prefixed Lump Sum Grants, each event should be one work package.
Work packages covering financial support to third parties must describe the conditions for implementing the support.
Limit the number of work packages and reduce deliverables (max 20 for the entire project).
Enter each activity/milestone/output/outcome/deliverable only once (under one work package).
Ensure consistency with the detailed budget table/calculator and Part A.

sub.label: 5.1 Ethics and EU values
prompts: Describe ethics issues that may arise during the project implementation and the measures you intend to take to solve/avoid them.
Describe how you will ensure gender and non-discrimination mainstreaming in the project cycle.
Gender and non-discrimination mainstreaming means integrating gender equality and non-discrimination considerations in the design, implementation, monitoring and evaluation of project activities.
Projects activities should be pro-active and contribute to the equal empowerment of women and men, girls and boys, in all their diversity.
Ensure that they achieve their full potential, enjoy the same rights and opportunities.
If your project has a direct or indirect impact on children and their rights, indicate it clearly.
Ensure that your project is based on a child rights approach following the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights and the UN Convention on the Rights of the Child.
Address children as rights holders and ensure their participation in the design and implementation of the project.
If you will have direct contacts with children, provide child protection policies in line with the Keeping Children Safe Child Safeguarding Standards.
Explain how you intend to address privacy/data protection issues related to data collection, analysis and dissemination.
Outline measures to guarantee compliance with the EU values mentioned in Article 2 of the Treaty on the European Union and Article 21 of the EU Charter of Fundamental Rights.

sub.label: 5.2 Security
prompts: Address any security issues relevant to your project.
Describe whether your activity involves EU classified information (EUCI).
Describe whether your activity has the potential for misuse of results.
Describe any other security issues that should be taken into consideration.

sub.label: 6.1 Double funding
prompts: Confirm that neither the project as a whole nor any parts of it have benefitted from any other EU grant.
Confirm that neither the project nor any parts of it are (nor will be) submitted for any other EU grant.
Note: There is a strict prohibition of double funding from the EU budget.

sub.label: 6.2 Financial support to third parties
prompts: If in your project the maximum amount per third party will be more than the threshold amount set in the Call document, justify and explain why the higher amount is necessary to fulfil your project's objectives.
